evidences.text: Update: In case you want to have a more simplified version of this article, please check out BlackEnergy trojan strikes again: Attacks Ukrainian electric power industry .
ESET has recently discovered that the BlackEnergy trojan was recently used as a backdoor to deliver a destructive KillDisk component in attacks against
Furthermore, we examine a previously unknown SSH backdoor that was also used as another channel of accessing the infected systems, in addition to BlackEnergy.
This value is a unique text string used to identify individual infections or infection attempts by the BlackEnergy malware
KillDisk component In 2014 some variants of the BlackEnergy trojan contained a plugin designed for the destruction of the infected system, named dstr.
In 2015 the BlackEnergy group started to use a new destructive BlackEnergy component detected by ESET products as Win32/KillDisk.NBB,
Once activated, this variant of the KillDisk component looks for and terminates two non-standard processes with the following names: komut.exe sec_service.exe
We didn’t manage to find any information regarding the name of the first process (komut.exe).
